newsitem.title: GERMANY: IMI Sigeco says reaffirms VW as buy.
newsitem.headline: IMI Sigeco says reaffirms VW as buy.

text.p: IMI Sigeco analyst Sabine Bluemel said on Thursday that she has reaffirmed her earnings estimates for Volkswagen AG and looked for shares in the German carmaker to keep up their recent strong performance.

"We expect the VW group to report a steady increase in profits driven by volume growth on the back of new model introductions and cost cutting," Bluemel said in a report that confirmed her buy recommendation.
Bluemel said she estimated DVFA earnings per share for 1997 at 71 marks, 1998 at 105 marks and 1999 at 132 marks compared with 55 marks in 1996.
The share has already reached her price target of 1,500 marks, having risen 35 percent since the beginning of May and outperformed the DAX index.

"As the group continues to apply extremely conservative accounting methods, it should continue to understate underlying profitability, which should be reflected in high DVFA adjustments of more than one billion marks in 1997 and 1998," Bluemel said.
She also said VW would likely reach the lower end of its profitability target of 6.5 percent pre-tax return on sales by the year 2000.
VW shares have been trading in unchartered territory since January when they broke a seven-year historic high at 643 marks.
She said VW shares should continue to benefit from expected further strength of the DAX index in the medium-term and the mark's weakness against the dollar.

Another factor she cited was that VW shares remain the most undervalued in the sector given future earnings growth, trading at a 28 percent discount to the European sector and a 32 percent discount to other European companies.
